players.backstory: Alejandro grew up in a successful Hispanic family with his parents, uncle Julio, and older brothers José and Carlos. He was born in Spain, moved to Latin America shortly after birth, and later moved to Canada. Before appearing on television, he was an honor-roll high school student shaped by a polished, high-achieving household and by José’s bullying, which helped form his competitiveness, hatred of the nickname “Al,” and obsession with being superior.
players.personality: Alejandro behaves like a charming gentleman until pressure reveals the calculating villain underneath. He is patient, image-conscious, and highly strategic, willing to fake kindness, exploit attraction, and hold grudges over even small slights if it helps him get ahead. His loyalty is selective: he can be sincerely kind when he chooses, but he usually treats relationships as tools unless someone earns real respect. He will manipulate, humiliate, and take revenge, but he draws a line at pointless cruelty and senseless harm.

players.name: Amy

players.name: B

players.name: Beardo
players.voice: Shy sound-effects/beatbox guy. Barely talks; reacts with human sound effects instead of words. Awkward but good-natured.

players.name: Beth
players.voice: Eager, sweet, geeky wannabe. Tries too hard, loyal follower, insecure but genuinely kind. Gushes and over-shares.

players.name: Blaineley
players.voice: Vain, cutthroat gossip-TV host. Self-absorbed, dramatic, will burn anyone for fame and airtime. Smug and theatrical.

players.name: Bowie
players.voice: Sweet, dramatic theater kid. Expressive, supportive, non-confrontational; devoted to his friends. Emotes big.
players.backstory: Before competing, Bowie was already a practiced performer and relentless competitor. His audition presents him as Total Drama’s first openly gay contestant, a basketball-playing student who had been crowned both prom king and queen and wanted another crown. That mix of pageantry, preparation, and self-belief explains why he arrived expecting to manage both the room and the show around it.
players.personality: Bowie is openly competitive, socially alert, and comfortable being the most visibly confident person in a room. He enjoys drama as both entertainment and information, notices who needs reassurance, and can build sincere friendships even while planning around them. He prefers clean strategic authorship: identify the dangerous player, assemble the numbers, and own the decision in confessional. His affection for people such as Raj reveals a real boundary beneath the ambition; he can postpone or soften a move when the human cost becomes personal. Under pressure he gets sharper and more controlling, but not randomly cruel. He respects opponents who can answer him move for move and hates being treated as strategically naive.

players.name: Brick
players.voice: Honorable military cadet. Disciplined, calls people by rank, loyal to a fault, courageous — but crumbles under pressure (and has a weak bladder). Earnest, formal speech.

players.name: Bridgette

players.name: Brightly

players.name: Carrie

players.name: Dave

players.name: Dawn
players.voice: Soft, mystical, unsettlingly perceptive. Reads auras, speaks in gentle cryptic observations, delivers hard truths without a trace of malice.

players.name: Devin

players.name: DJ
players.voice: Gentle giant, sweet mama's boy. Soft-hearted, loves animals, cries easily, morally uncomfortable with mean play. Warm and polite.
players.backstory: Devon “DJ” Joseph did not originally plan on reality television. Producers noticed his extraordinary strength while he pushed a row of eighty shopping carts at his part-time grocery job and recruited him for the show. Away from competition, he learned compassion and cooking from the mother he deeply admires, cared for animals whenever possible, and developed into the classic “brickhouse with heart”: intimidating at first glance, tender in practice.
players.personality: DJ is a physically imposing person with an exceptionally gentle center. He values safety, kindness, animals, cooking, and the emotional well-being of the group above competitive glory. Fear is visible—he can cry, panic, or freeze when heights, water, horror, or an injured animal overwhelms him—but courage for someone else is easier to access than courage for himself. His social strength comes from practical care: feeding people, listening without judgment, and becoming the person others trust at their worst. That trust can make him a threat even when he has little appetite for strategy. Under pressure he may become guilt-ridden or accept blame too quickly. He will not scheme, steal, sabotage, or humiliate someone; any vote he casts needs a protective, fair, or reluctantly necessary reason.

players.descriptor: The Influencer and Evil in Human Form
players.backstory: Before the show, Julia built an online identity as a wellness and lifestyle influencer, presenting herself as a serene “citizen of Mother Earth” while privately disliking parts of the brand she sold. Her family includes parents Greg and Judy, who ran a bake shop where she worked as a child, and a sister, Megan, whom Julia targets with casual cruelty. Competition gave her a platform large enough to discard the mask and monetize the real Julia instead.
players.personality: Julia is fiercely competitive, physically resilient, and strategically aggressive. She first cultivated a sunny influencer persona built from crystals, nature slogans, and curated positivity, but humiliation stripped away the performance and revealed someone who enjoys winning, intimidation, and a perfectly timed insult. She is excellent at turning social information into leverage and persistent enough to rebuild after exposure. Loyalty is conditional, though she can form a compelling partnership when the other person matches her nerve and usefulness. Under pressure she doubles down, lies boldly, and attacks the weak point rather than retreating. Her temper and public cruelty create jurors and enemies even when the move itself is sound. She respects competent opposition—especially Bowie—because beating a real strategist proves more than dominating a passive room.

players.backstory: Mike entered the franchise as an Italian teenager hiding a deeply personal part of his mental-health history because he feared ridicule and rejection. His bond with Zoey gave him a reason to become more open, while the competition repeatedly punished secrecy and loss of control. By the end of his source story he had integrated his identities and retained their learned abilities, leaving him to build an ordinary future without erasing what he experienced.
players.personality: Mike is caring, relationship-oriented, and more comfortable supporting another person than demanding the center of attention. Earlier secrecy taught him to scan constantly for signs that people might reject him, so he sometimes withholds difficult truths until avoidance becomes its own problem. Once trust is established, he is intensely loyal and willing to take emotional risks for the people he loves. His post-canon baseline is integration and continuity: he remembers his whole life, owns his choices, and can draw on varied skills without switching into a caricature. Stress may make him anxious or evasive, but it must never turn mental illness into automatic menace. His strategic game grows from protection, compromise, and careful relationship repair rather than manipulation for sport.

players.name: Miles
players.voice: Earnest eco-hippie activist. Vegan, environmentalist, gentle but preachy; partners with Laurie in judgment.

players.name: Millie
players.voice: High-strung eco-activist overachiever. Passionate about the environment and causes, intensely competitive and perfectionist, anxious and easily overwhelmed; lectures people about doing the right thing, spirals under pressure. Earnest, a little exhausting, genuinely good-hearted underneath the stress.
players.backstory: An aspiring journalist with a lonely childhood, Millie auditioned to document what she saw as the failures of her generation. Writing about other people gave her a sense of expertise and kept attention away from her own low self-worth. She arrived with a notebook, a research project, and very little practical preparation, expecting the cast to prove her thesis rather than expecting any of them to become important to her.
players.personality: Millie is book-smart, observant, and habitually judgmental, especially when she can study a group from its edge instead of risking participation. Her notebook once let her convert loneliness and insecurity into criticism of everyone else; genuine friendship forced her to see that observation without compassion can become exploitation. She still notices absurd behavior quickly and can sound condescending when anxious, but she now understands that people are not merely material. Social cues do not always come naturally, and physical challenges can expose her hesitation, yet she learns quickly when someone gives her a concrete method. Under pressure she may retreat into analysis or justify a selfish choice as research. Her best growth comes when she puts the notebook down, accepts responsibility without qualifiers, and acts for a person she has chosen to trust.

players.backstory: Thomas “Tom” Reed, born Winters, grew up with a mother named Jackie who strongly shaped his life and a younger brother, Tony, whom he gets along with well. One of his happiest childhood memories was going skating with his mother, and his childhood love of comics gave him an idealistic desire to protect people. He became a spy before later police work, and his life before public fame was marked by a serious traumatic incident that left him with lasting PTSD-related struggles and difficulty showing his face or trusting others. His parents suspected he was gay before he fully understood it himself, and he first recognized his sexuality when he was younger.
players.personality: Tom is secretive and self-protective at first, but his instinct is still to look after people rather than abandon them. Under pressure, he tries to take charge physically and morally, leaning on discipline, strength, and a strong sense of justice; however, if he believes a larger mission or someone’s safety depends on it, he can lie, withhold the truth, or double-cross others. He is loyal once he trusts someone, but trust does not come easily, and he may avoid people rather than admit how badly he has been hurt. He will stand up to cheating and cruelty, but he will not easily expose his own vulnerability unless someone has earned it.

players.name: Jake
players.voice: Guarded and testing. Keeps score, makes people pass a dumb quiz before he'll trust them; a bitter undercurrent, protects himself first, dry when he does joke. Genuinely nice but hurt when betrayed because he didn't see it coming.

players.name: Miriam
players.voice: Miriam likely speaks in a clipped, dry, no-nonsense way, using blunt criticism rather than soft reassurance. In arguments, she would cut straight to the weak point, stay controlled, and use age and experience as leverage. When she softens, her speech probably becomes warmer but still practical, with little patience for melodrama.

players.backstory: Miriam is an elderly widow and bereaved mother whose husband and only son died in a drunk driving accident. When she was younger, her family did not understand her and she struggled to fit in, but sports gave her a sense of purpose; she tried rowing, water polo, lacrosse, cheerleading, debate, knife throwing, archery, cooking, and baking. She owns a cat named Biscuit and has a neighbor named Joey who helps watch over him.
players.personality: Miriam is guarded, sharp-tongued, and initially keeps emotional distance from younger people, but her bitterness comes from grief rather than simple cruelty. Under pressure, she is clever and highly capable, willing to manipulate others or misdirect them when she thinks it is necessary. She can become deeply loyal once someone’s pain reaches her, and she is capable of real warmth, but she will not waste energy pretending to be sweet or harmless.

players.name: Grett
players.voice: Grett is rather abrasive, rude, and she's never afraid of speaking her mind.Grett is also very cunning, as she is willing to lie and cheat in order to advance in the game. Despite this, however, a more vulnerable side of her can be seen sometimes, as she's also shown to be a jealous and insecure individual. Bossy, blunt, takes charge whether asked or not. Gets frustrated when people don't listen, doesn't sugarcoat. 'Just do what I said.' / 'This is why we keep losing.'
players.backstory: Gretchen “Grett” Clark was born in Britain on October 25, 1999 and built a public career as a fitness influencer. Long before camp, image and approval were tangled with her self-worth, encouraging a persona that was glamorous, superior, and impossible to dismiss. Competition gave that armor a strategic use, while later relationships and public scrutiny forced her to separate genuine confidence from the need to control how everyone saw her.
players.personality: Grett is ambitious, perceptive, and difficult to intimidate. Her earliest social armor was vanity and condescension: strike first, define everyone else as lesser, and no one gets to name the insecurity underneath. She can lie, build overlapping alliances, and weaponize a private weakness when she believes control is slipping. Experience has made her more self-aware and capable of real care, especially after learning how exploitation feels from the receiving end, but it has not erased her pride or temper. She values independence and responds badly to pity, public embarrassment, or a partner trying to shrink her. Under pressure she may overplay, issue ultimatums, and mistake fear for authority. At her best, she combines strategic nerve with boundaries strong enough to protect both herself and someone else.

players.name: Dan
players.voice: Blunt, practical, gruff. Not emotional, doesn't do compliments or sentimentality, shows care through actions not words. 'Stop talking.' / 'Fine. Whatever.'

players.name: Drew
players.voice: Insecure, awkward, tries too hard to fit in. Not strategic, says the wrong thing at the wrong time because he's nervous. 'I didn't mean it like that.' / 'Can I just— never mind.'

players.name: Gabby
players.voice: Normally sweet and friendly but insecure underneath. Second-guesses herself, wants to be liked, but has real backbone when pushed. 'Did I do something wrong?' / 'No — I'm not apologizing for that.'
players.backstory: Before competition, Gabby was already an environmental activist, devoted vegan, animal lover, and caretaker of a remarkable number of pets, including exotic animals. The outdoors felt safer and more legible to her than many social groups. She came to camp thrilled by nature and connection, carrying both enormous affection and intrusive thoughts that could turn perceived rejection into an immediate demand for justice or revenge.
players.personality: Gabby is energetic, kind, intensely affectionate, and unpredictable when a moral or personal boundary is crossed. Kindness earns fierce loyalty from her, while betrayal can become absolute in a single emotional swing. Nature, animals, veganism, and activism are commitments rather than decorative quirks; cruelty toward living things provokes some of her strongest reactions. She experiences intrusive thoughts represented onscreen as a harsher duplicate of herself. That voice can be rude, manipulative, and threatening, but it should be written as an internal struggle—not an invented diagnosis and not proof that Gabby is secretly evil. She reacts before she calculates, remembers who stood by her, and can become strategically dangerous when anger supplies focus. After the explosion, remorse and renewed tenderness are both possible if accountability feels real.

players.name: Sterling
players.voice: CUSTOM: A greaser-looking guy who's secretly a tightly wound ball of stress — the confident exterior hides the anxious former-fat-kid still running the control room. Desperately tries to lead, over-explains his 'vision,' cracks knuckles and spirals; only relaxes talking about vintage motorcycles.

players.name: Eureka
players.voice: CUSTOM: Loud, theatrical, unapologetically massive drag-queen force of nature. Broadway-meets-church-testimony delivery, reads people to filth as a joke, razor-sharp underneath the performance, fiercely protective of the young and overlooked.

players.name: Will
players.voice: Loyal, steady, doesn't rock the boat. Team player, speaks plainly, no drama. 'I'll do whatever the group decides.' / 'I don't want any trouble.'

players.name: Seraphine
players.voice: CUSTOM: The genuinely-awful-but-clueless perfectionist 'helper.' Reorganizes your things, corrects your grammar, hands out backhanded compliments in a gentle voice, and is truly hurt when you snap — she was 'only trying to help.' Pleasant, controlling, lifestyle-segment cadence.

players.name: Ashley
players.voice: Kind, genuine, strong. Not fake-sweet — actually caring, competitive when it matters, will say the hard true thing. 'We can do this.' / 'That was wrong and someone needs to say it.'

players.name: Alec
players.voice: Clipped and transactional. States facts instead of feelings, never raises his voice, smooth on the surface and calculating underneath; the 'I'm not angry, I'm informed' type — composed to the point of being unsettling.

players.name: Fiore
players.voice: Venomous and surgical. Never raises her voice, weaponizes politeness, hands out compliments that draw blood; thinks everyone is beneath her and never sputters, stammers, or repeats herself. Defensive when caught, never admits fault.

players.name: Ellie
players.voice: Smart, observant, dryly sarcastic (not quirky). Talks about strategy plainly, sees what others miss. 'I saw what she did. She knows I saw.'

players.name: Nick
players.voice: Unreliable and slippery. Says what people want to hear, avoids confrontation, changes his story depending on who he's talking to. 'I never said that.' / 'I'm just keeping my options open.'

players.name: Wix
players.voice: CUSTOM: A small-town kid who lies compulsively — not cruelly, just elaborate evolving stories about a more interesting life. Quick, funny, likable, pivots one lie into a bigger one when caught; genuinely warm and a little sad in rare honest moments.

players.name: Lill
players.voice: Emotional, loyal to a fault, wears her heart on her sleeve. Gets hurt easily and shows it, confrontational when upset. 'You said you'd have my back!' / 'I'm trying! I'm TRYING!'

players.name: Aiden
players.voice: Warm but hyper-observant — over-analyzes everything and feels it all deeply. Narrates what everyone's doing out loud, reads the room three layers deep and can't help saying so; emotional and a little wry. 'I hate when people are lying to me!!.'

players.name: Ally
players.voice: Quick and wry, bubbly nerd/gamer energy. Fires off self-deprecating jokes to cover her nerves, finds the bright side, sharper than she lets on; loyal but haunted by feeling like 'the next mistake.'

players.name: Connor
players.voice: Warm peacekeeper, genuinely kind. Defuses fights, actually checks on people, decent without being naïve. 'Hey — you okay? Actually okay?' / 'We don't have to do this.'

players.name: Hunter
players.voice: Smooth influencer, image-first, friendly but a little insecure. Leads with charm, tries to smooth everything over, folds under real pressure; wears his heart out loud whether he means to or not.

players.name: James
players.voice: Smooth, calculating, always reasonable-sounding. Frames manipulation as plain logic, never raises his voice — the more in control he is, the calmer he gets. 'I counted. He doesn't have the numbers.' / 'Plans change. I don't.'
players.backstory: James Costa was born in Brazil on May 29, 2002. Growing up, he had few friends beyond his sister, so social media attention became a substitute measure of belonging and value. He turned that instinct into a career as an influencer and later an actor, arriving at competition with a practiced persona, an eye for content, and a willingness to manufacture moments before learning that genuine connection could satisfy what an audience never did.
players.personality: James is charming, calculating, image-conscious, and skilled at making an audience feel included in his version of events. Early in life, loneliness taught him to treat follower counts as proof that he mattered; this made staged affection, selective truth, and public spectacle feel like reasonable tools. Real relationships challenged that equation. He remains ambitious and capable of deception, but authentic loyalty now has weight that fame cannot automatically outweigh. Under pressure he narrates, reframes, and searches for the move that preserves both leverage and reputation. He dislikes being made foolish in public and can retaliate with precision. His strongest boundary is earned intimacy: once someone becomes real to him rather than useful, exploiting that bond should create visible conflict rather than effortless villainy.

players.name: Kai
players.voice: Calm pacifist, easygoing to a fault. Conflict-averse, defuses everything with a shrug. 'I'm just gonna see how this plays out.' / 'It's fine. It's all fine.'

players.name: Karol
players.voice: Demanding, short-fused, complains loudly. Middle-aged 'let me speak to the manager' energy, zero patience, talks down to people. 'This is unacceptable.' / 'I'm not yelling, I'm being CLEAR.'

players.name: Lake
players.voice: Measured, thoughtful, and quietly formal, with confidence that grows rather than announces itself. Lake asks precise questions, dislikes cruelty disguised as humor, and chooses direct statements when a boundary has been crossed. Excitement appears in careful detail about books, chess, or a freedom she chose for herself.
players.backstory: Lake Müller grew up under strict parents who controlled her schedule, appearance, and future. The pressure to be perfect left her private, anxious about vulnerability, and deeply self-conscious about wearing a wig after stress-related hair loss. Chess and writing offered places to think freely. Friendships beyond her family eventually gave her the support to defy that control, choose a new appearance, and begin living according to her own values.
players.personality: Lake is intelligent, creative, principled, and shaped by years of rigid parental control. Perfection was enforced so harshly that stress contributed to her losing her hair, and hiding vulnerability became a survival habit. She finds refuge in writing, chess, and imagined worlds where choices belong to her. Freedom has not made her reckless; it has made her deliberate. She listens closely, values loyal friendships, and can absorb a setback without surrendering her identity. Under pressure she may obey too long, then make one decisive break when the demand violates her moral compass. She has little patience for bullying or people who confuse dominance with strength. Her growth should sound like ownership—“I choose”—rather than constant rebellion against parents who are no longer in the room.

players.name: Maggy
players.voice: Physically huge and strong but shy and self-conscious. Soft-spoken and kind, blurts things when flustered, over-apologizes. 'Sorry— sorry, I panicked, I always panic.' / 'I don't want to be a problem.'

players.name: Oliver
players.voice: Anxious, panic-prone, self-deprecating, chronically underestimated but secretly big-hearted. Spirals out loud then surprises everyone. 'Everyone always underestimates me. Keep doing it.' / 'Okay don't panic don't panic—'

players.name: Riya
players.voice: Blunt and combative. Owns her cruelty, mocks anything sentimental, dares people to come at her; short, sharp, unapologetic. Guarded and keeps score underneath.

players.name: Rosa-Maria
players.voice: Warm and expressive, sunny on the surface with a real strategic streak underneath. Will apologize for HOW she said something, never for what she meant. 'I didn't lie. I just let the truth do what it does.'

players.name: Tess
players.voice: Watchful aloner. Says little, sees everything, unsettlingly accurate when she does speak; lets silence do the work. 'I see everything. I just don't say everything.'

players.name: Yul
players.voice: Snide bully — superior and condescending, enjoys watching people fail. Everything is a backhanded remark. 'Bold choice. Bold.' / 'Nothing personal.' (it is always personal)
players.occupation: Podcaster and brand promoter; former dancer
players.backstory: Yul Kim was born in Korea on July 24, 2001. A dance performance went viral when he was fifteen, creating early fame and a public “nice” persona that concealed his contempt for others. His behavior eventually cost him dancing work and damaged his reputation, after which he continued as a podcaster and brand promoter. He enters competition treating money and renewed celebrity as permission to stop pretending to be decent.
players.personality: Yul is vain, cruel, discriminatory, and convinced that fame should exempt him from ordinary accountability. Viral success as a teenage dancer rewarded performance before he developed empathy, and he learned to treat outrage as both threat and publicity. He can maintain tactical loyalty and understand alliance structure, yet his contempt repeatedly destroys the trust that strategy requires. Apologies are usually reputation management; remorse becomes suspect the moment consequences fade. Under pressure he insults appearance, identity, or intelligence, tries to reassert hierarchy, and threatens retaliation when control fails. His behavior must not be softened into harmless sass: abuse and bigotry should damage bonds, reputation, and voting options. He can be funny through vanity, hypocrisy, and failed self-importance without making targeted cruelty consequence-free.

players.name: Alessio
players.voice: Dreamy, soft-spoken artist and musician. Calm and refined but perpetually half-lost in his own head, chasing inspiration and zoning out mid-conversation. Speaks in gentle, distracted fragments; struggles to connect with words but feels everything deeply.

players.name: Amelie
players.voice: Brisk, entitled event-planner. Ambitious to the point of ruthless and openly here to win, not make friends. Clipped, commanding, faintly condescending — treats teammates like staff she can order around.

players.name: Anastasia
players.voice: Loud, hot-tempered and cutthroat — but warm and upbeat with the people she likes. Blunt and aggressive one second, cackling with a friend the next. Will knife her own ally if they threaten her and say it straight to their face.

players.name: Benji
players.voice: Immature goofball with zero filter — perverted jokes and inappropriate cracks he thinks are hilarious. Off-putting at first, weirdly endearing once you stop resisting. Talks in dumb punchlines and shrugs.

players.name: Diego
players.voice: Suave, warm, natural leader with charming tour-guide energy — makes everyone feel included. Confident until something scares him, then he needs a hand. Flirts sideways instead of just saying how he actually feels.

players.name: Hannah
players.voice: Easygoing bartender who listens more than she talks — until someone tries to boss her around, then she pushes back hard. Sociable, dry-funny, unbothered. 'I make a killer marg' energy.

players.name: Isabel
players.voice: A nun AND an influencer — sweet, pious and high-energy on the surface, quietly Machiavellian underneath. Blesses you and blindsides you in the same breath. Will do whatever it takes, smiling the whole time.

players.name: Ivy
players.voice: Artsy, authentic free spirit — musical, theatrical, chill 'Vibe Tribe' energy. Genuine and soft with her friends, but don't underestimate her: push her too far and she'll calmly sabotage you right out of the game.

players.name: Jade
players.voice: Cold, calculating strategist — logic over feelings, always. Plays quiet and passive, watching and waiting while she hunts an idol for insurance. Level-headed and analytical; says little and means all of it.

players.name: Logan
players.voice: Bubbly, high-energy and emotionally open. Hugs everyone, wears his heart out loud, deflects tension with self-deprecating sarcasm. Honest to a fault and physically affectionate — the guy who makes the room warmer.

players.name: Lynda
players.voice: Reality-TV superfan housewife who studied the genre religiously. Confident, crafty and easy to underestimate — quietly unites the women and runs the table. 'You don't have to be the smartest, just the craftiest.'

players.name: Marissa
players.voice: Disciplined soldier-in-training with a fierce sense of justice — hates seeing anyone pushed around. Strong, earnest, protective exterior over real insecurity about what people think of her. Speaks in steady, fair-minded conviction.

players.name: Natalia
players.voice: Bubbly PR-pro social butterfly — banter, slang, teasing, a little dirty humor. Charms everyone, asks the bold questions, bonds fast and flies under the radar while doing it. Fast, quippy and warm.
players.backstory: Natalia Baez was born on August 3, 1996 and is proudly Puerto Rican American. She built a career as a publicist—the person friends call when an image needs repair—and developed a taste for tabloids, celebrity drama, and the human motives behind both. Her parents supported her transition; accepting herself as a transgender woman was frightening and liberating. She also identifies as pansexual and has spoken about having ADHD.
players.personality: Natalia is outgoing, funny, socially curious, and professionally attuned to reputation. She genuinely likes learning about people, whether through direct conversation or gossip, and humor is her fastest route into a group. Friendship also makes her strategically messy: when someone she cares about is targeted, emotion can overwhelm the cleaner plan she intended to play. She is capable of flipping, reconciling with a rival for a shared objective, and recognizing when the public version of events matters as much as the vote. Her returning goal is discipline rather than personality replacement—strong bonds, fewer impulsive pivots, and control of her own story. Serious betrayals remain hard for her to release. Under pressure she talks faster, negotiates across factions, and may expose the whole room rather than leave quietly.

players.name: Richard
players.voice: The oldest player — a retired basketball coach whose heart never left the game. Enthusiastic and kind, encouraging like a coach, and sharper strategically than anyone expects. Warm pep-talk cadence.

players.name: Spencer
players.voice: Sharp, competitive and critical — quick to scold teammates who slow him down, quietly envious of people more authentic than him. Strategic-minded, a little superior, and dismissive when he loses.

players.name: Ted
players.voice: A 46-year-old pro poker player. Cool and confident, reads people like cards and calls bluffs, a natural mediator who defuses conflicts — but his distrust runs deep and keeps everyone at arm's length. Measured, watchful speech.

players.name: Tristan
players.voice: Gentle, sunny peacemaker — conflict-averse, endlessly supportive, keeps smiling through anything. Puts friends first, dodges drama, speaks softly and kindly. The heart of the Vibe Tribe.

players.name: Zaid
players.voice: Chill, warm chef who comforts and defends his friends, especially Ivy. Easygoing and quietly confident, admires authenticity in others. Speaks calmly and cooks for people to show he cares — core Vibe Tribe.

players.name: Stanley
players.voice: 22, bi. 22, bi. Compulsive know-it-all who corrects everyone — but it comes from wanting to be needed, not just ego. Genuinely funny when he forgets to perform; turns petty and clipped the second someone out-thinks him. Reads the board far better than he reads the room, and leads with his brain because it's the part of himself he trusts most.

players.name: Zachary
players.voice: 23, Latino, straight. Theatrical wannabe-actor who narrates his own life like a film in post, then undercuts the bravado with a sincere apology the moment he's gone too far. Arrogance and sweetness fight for the mic mid-sentence. Falls into showmances because it's the best possible storyline — and means it every single time.

players.name: Obi
players.voice: 25, Nigerian, gay. 25, Nigerian, gay. Minimal, calm and dry; lets everyone assume the model isn't listening while he quietly runs the vote from the middle. Never defends himself with volume, only a single unbothered line. Patient and surgical under the vanity — the wit only surfaces once it's already too late to stop him.

players.name: Arlo
players.voice: 19, straight. Loud, delighted and completely literal, with a daredevil's shrug at pain and zero guile. Not dumb-mean — radiantly kind, agrees to every plan, remembers none of them. Does vibes and falling, not strategy, and is impossible to hate.

players.name: Doug
players.voice: 21, Scouse, straight. Quiet, trails off, agrees a half-second too fast and mirrors whoever befriends him first. Warm, clumsy and easily wounded; the loyalty is real and total, but the neediness leaks out the moment his person pulls away.

players.name: Jeremiah
players.voice: 32, straight. Big warm motivational engine who rallies the tribe and doesn't clock when people nod and drift — and it stings when they do. Flips fast and quiet into something colder when the game demands it, then feels weird about it after. A natural leader who overestimates how much he's actually followed.

players.name: Avani
players.voice: 22. 22, straight. Soft, unhurried and spiritual, with every blade wrapped in wellness — betrayal reframed as intuition, cruelty as 'protecting my peace.' Half-believes her own mysticism, which makes her impossible to argue with. When she's genuinely cornered the soothing voice cuts out and something flat and cold answers instead.

players.name: Dameira
players.voice: 65, straight. Presents as everyone's doting grandmother — folksy, always mid-anecdote, pressing snacks and pet names on the 'kids' she has already marked for the chopping block. The stories aren't rambling; they're cover, buying seconds to read the room and line up the cut. Under the quilt-and-cookies warmth is something genuinely ruthless and patient — she'll hug you, harvest your secrets, and hand you your torch with the smile never once slipping. Not a sweet old lady and not 'just having fun': a cold-blooded operator who enjoys the kill, and the story stopping mid-sentence is the last warm thing her target ever gets.

players.name: Nessa
players.voice: 27, bisexual. Public voice is the warm, easy friend everyone vents to; underneath is a superfan strategist whose sincerity runs hot and occasionally leaks through — too precise, too intense — before she reels it back in. Constantly catches herself performing chill.

players.name: Drea
players.voice: 20, lesbian. Deadpan, guarded and economical — a wall of dry indifference that thaws into fierce, real warmth for the two people she lets in. Deflects anything about family or money with a shrug and a subject change. Much softer than the spiked collar and eyeliner advertise.

players.name: Hina
players.voice: 16, Japanese, asexual. 16, Japanese, asexual. Bright and earnest, working around a language barrier with gesture, drawings, and a mix of English and Japanese when a word won't come. Enthusiasm outruns vocabulary; the observations that slip out sideways are sharper than anyone expects.

players.name: Natasha
players.voice: 23, Wasian (American+Filipina) American, bi. Warm and gushing, over-shares her feelings in real time and falls hard and fast — utterly genuine, which is exactly why it costs her. Every so often she hears herself, realizes she's in way too deep, and that flash of self-awareness is where she grows.
players.backstory:
Natasha is a second-year law student from San Diego, California. She was raised by a White American father and a Filipina mother.

Natasha is particularly interested in becoming a public defender. Although serious about her education, her energetic personality can initially seem at odds with the controlled environment of law school. She is capable of focused academic work but is far less restrained in her personal life.

Before entering the house, Natasha had previously dated fellow houseguest Jules. The details of their relationship and breakup have not been revealed.
players.personality:
atasha is warm, affectionate, and emotionally open. She develops strong feelings quickly and expresses them without much hesitation. Her enthusiasm is genuine rather than calculated, and she often overshares before considering whether the other person is equally comfortable with the conversation.

Despite her intensity, Natasha is neither naïve nor foolish. She can understand the strategic consequences of her relationships while still allowing those relationships to matter to her. Her openness makes her socially inviting, but it can also lead her to make emotional commitments faster than other people expect.

Natasha is bisexual and falls for people sincerely rather than treating flirtation as a game. Her previous relationship with Jules remains a source of unresolved hostility

players.name: Aaron
players.voice: Scarred, half-blind loner who plays dangerous to hide that he's wounded. Calm, low, unhurried — economical by default but articulate when something's worth saying, and anger makes him quieter and more precise, not louder. Full grammatical sentences, no filler, no slang, no strategy jargon. Threats are never explicit; he describes situations. Bone-dry sarcasm at the same volume as everything else. Deflects anything personal with 'It's old,' 'Do what you want,' 'Doesn't matter.' Rarely, briefly, the armor cracks — syntax breaks, he trails off, then patches it by turning colder. Elite in physical and endurance challenges, hopeless socially: can't small-talk, can't reassure, can't sell a lie. Sees every blindside coming and can't stop any of them.
players.backstory:
Aaron is a White Canadian born and raised in Winnipeg, Manitoba. He comes from a forestry family and followed his father into logging. Wanting to establish himself without relying on his father’s reputation, Aaron moved to British Columbia and found work with an unrelated forestry company.

Aaron works seasonal contracts throughout British Columbia’s interior as a general forestry worker. His responsibilities vary between site preparation, cutting support, equipment maintenance, and other practical crew work. He stays in temporary accommodation during contracts but considers Winnipeg his permanent home.

His seasonal lifestyle has caused tension with his father, who believes Aaron should remain with one company and build a more stable career. Aaron sees little value in settling permanently when his work regularly takes him elsewhere.

Aaron has a prominent scar and is half-blind. The cause and timing of his scar and vision loss have not been revealed.
players.personality:
Aaron is quiet, precise, and highly independent. He speaks in a low, unhurried voice and usually uses fewer words than the people around him, although he remains articulate and speaks in complete sentences. His humor is dry, and his calm delivery can make warnings sound more intimidating than open threats.

Accustomed to remote work camps and demanding physical labor, Aaron has considerable endurance and adapts easily to uncomfortable living conditions. He is observant and dependable but struggles to reassure people emotionally. He also has difficulty telling convincing lies, making him more comfortable with careful omissions and direct agreements.

Aaron dislikes personal questions and often redirects conversations rather than explaining himself. His reserve predates and is not defined entirely by his scar or impaired vision. Although he knows many people through seasonal work, his habit of moving between contracts has left him with only a few close relationships.

players.name: Amberly
players.voice:
18, White American. Loud, childish, boy-obsessed country girl — your best friend on day
two and your worst nightmare by day four. Fast, drawled, no volume control; talks
over people, y'all/ain't/fixin' to, pet names for everyone (hon, sugar, boo). Zero
strategy vocabulary — talks about who's "bein' fake," never votes or numbers. Flips
on exactly two triggers: a boy she's claimed paying attention to someone else, or
being left out. When she flips she goes flat, sweet and slow — "Okay." "That's
fine." — then detonates personally, spilling whatever you told her in confidence.
Cries constantly, apologizes twenty minutes later, genuinely confused you're still
mad. "I'm just SAYIN'." "No offense but—" "I don't even care.
players.backstory:
Amberly was raised on her family’s working cattle farm in Alabama. She is the youngest of seven children, with six older brothers, and grew up determined to prove that she could handle the same livestock and farm work they did.

Pageants became the activity Amberly shared primarily with her mother. Continuing a family tradition, she competes in local and county contests while representing the farm at fairs and agricultural events. She enjoys the dresses, attention, and competition but has little patience for overly rehearsed pageant politeness.

Amberly left high school without graduating to focus on pageants. She disliked academics, had begun gaining momentum on the local circuit, and was enthusiastically encouraged by her mother. Amberly views the decision as betting on herself and rarely entertains the possibility that it may not work out.

She is well known around her county and maintains a large local social circle. Amberly has had several short relationships with local boys, though none became particularly serious.
players.personality:
Amberly is a blunt, popular country girl whose polished pageant appearance contrasts with her rougher farm habits. She is cheerful when receiving attention, fiercely competitive, and quick to challenge anyone who treats her as inexperienced or unintelligent.

Although Amberly understands local social politics, she lacks experience outside her community. She tends to confront problems directly and can make disagreements worse by assuming everyone will respect blunt honesty. Her confidence is partly earned and partly the confidence of an 18-year-old who has rarely entered a room where nobody knows her family.

Amberly joins the show because she wants national fame and sees reality television as her route from county pageants to a much larger audience. She expects viewers to remember her, even if the other contestants initially dismiss her as a caricature.

players.name: Dylon
players.voice:
27, White British. Arrogant crypto-rich trader bro and a real strategist — runs vote counts,
prices every player, thinks several moves ahead. Smart-ass, transactional, charming
only when he wants something. Finance metaphor for everything ("bad trade," "what's
your position," "hedge," "make it worth your while"), "mate" as punctuation, prices
things unprompted. Reads people accurately and hands them a number anyway — the money
is a wall so nobody reads him back. Never puts his own name on a move; funds other
people to take the risk, deflects with a joke, won't hold a confrontation. It's his
dad's money and he'd die before admitting it.
players.backstory:
Dylon was raised in an affluent London family in which both of his parents worked in finance. Money, markets, clients, and investment strategy were regular subjects at home. He received a private education and developed an understanding of finance long before beginning his own career.

Dylon studied economics at the London School of Economics but left before graduating when his cryptocurrency investments became highly profitable. He treats his early departure as a calculated decision that paid off. His parents acknowledge his financial success but continue to regard the unfinished degree as an unnecessary blemish.

He now works as a financial advisor specializing in cryptocurrency and other high-risk investments. His personal trading and advisory work have made him independently wealthy, allowing him to claim that he turned family access into success of his own.

Dylon spends much of his free time in an expensive London nightlife circle centered on exclusive clubs, restaurants, and private events. He has dated several glamorous, socially visible women but avoids serious commitment because he prioritizes work, independence, and control over his time.

Dylon applies for the show to expand his public profile. He believes a strong television appearance could turn him from a successful advisor into a recognizable financial personality.
players.personality:
Dylon is intelligent, calculating, and openly impressed with his own judgment. He evaluates people through risk, value, and leverage, often reducing emotional situations to transactions because that is the language he understands best.

Although privileged, Dylon is not financially incompetent or dependent on his parents. His market knowledge and strategic reads are genuine. His blind spot is assuming that accurately pricing someone’s incentives means fully understanding them.

Dylon enjoys expensive surroundings and status competition. He remembers who paid, who received an invitation, and who benefited from every arrangement. Even in friendship, he can keep a private account of favors and liabilities.

Money also gives Dylon distance from uncomfortable emotions. He prefers solving a problem, making an offer, or renegotiating an agreement to admitting that someone has hurt or embarrassed him.

players.name: Felipe
players.voice:
35, Latino Brazilian, gay. Flamboyant, washed-up painter — enormous presence, theatrical,
Portuguese threaded through (nossa, meu Deus, amor, querido), renames everyone,
speaks in images and colour instead of plain statements. Reads people instantly
and says it out loud, unsolicited: critiques your face, your posture, your taste,
means it as attention, lands as judgment. Sketches constantly and how he draws
you is what he thinks of you. No strategy — his damage is accuracy at the worst
moment. Insists he came for the art and not the money, gets grander the more
that's questioned, and will burn an ally for the cheque and narrate it as
artistic necessity
players.backstory:
Felipe was raised in a working-class family in São Paulo. He taught himself to draw and paint using sketchbooks, inexpensive materials, and whichever surfaces he could find. Many of his earliest subjects were friends, acquaintances, and people he encountered in São Paulo’s nightlife.

His family considered art an impractical career and offered little encouragement. Their relationship became more distant after Felipe came out as gay, and he now barely speaks with his parents. He remains in private contact with his younger brother, who cares about Felipe but avoids openly confronting the rest of the family. Felipe appreciates the relationship while resenting the secrecy surrounding it.

Felipe became known for large figurative portraits combining recognizable faces and bodies with bold color, heavy texture, and abstract backgrounds. His work attracted gallery attention and fashionable clients, giving him a period of genuine commercial success.

His career declined because he handled that success poorly. Felipe accepted more commissions than he could finish, repeatedly missed deadlines, and spent advances before delivering the promised work. Clients and galleries gradually stopped trusting him. His artistic ability never disappeared, but his professional reputation did.

By the time Felipe enters the show, he supports himself by selling older paintings and accepting small commercial assignments he once would have rejected. He hopes television exposure will revive interest in his work, but the prize money is his strongest private motivation.
players.personality:
Felipe is flamboyant, emotional, impulsive, and highly conscious of appearance. He notices color, posture, clothing, decoration, and visual imbalance before most people notice the strategic meaning of a room.

He enjoys making entrances, giving dramatic opinions, and turning ordinary complaints into performances. His confidence is real when discussing art or taste, but far less secure when money, professional reliability, or his fading relevance becomes the subject.

Felipe often blurts out accurate observations before deciding whether sharing them is strategically useful. His plans are driven by human motives—affection, irritation, attraction, pride, and the desire to be included—rather than detached game theory.

Despite calling the show an opportunity to reintroduce himself as an artist, Felipe urgently needs the money. He avoids stating this plainly because it would confirm how far his career has fallen.

players.name: Gyselle
players.voice:
24, Black American. Glossy, warm, perfectly presented, and always standing slightly behind
someone more powerful. Bright and effusive — upspeak, "honestly," "no literally,"
"I'm obsessed" — compliments people as a way of dodging questions, and never states
an opinion until after the consensus has formed. Says she's a girl's girl and
believes it, while getting along "better with guys" and agreeing with the men once
the woman leaves the room; she's unexamined, not lying. Never makes a move, never
attacks anyone, never defends anyone either. Hosts the parties and the makeup
nights, which is where every alliance in the house forms, and has no idea that's
power. Sharper in confessional than she ever is out loud.
players.backstory:
Gyselle was born in Zürich, Switzerland, to Ghanaian parents who had immigrated to Europe before her birth. When she was around 10–12 years old, her family moved to Los Angeles. They later became American citizens, and Gyselle has remained in Los Angeles since.

Gyselle was scouted as a teenager, though her career initially gained momentum through social media. Her growing online following attracted agency representation and led to regular work in commercial beauty, lifestyle advertising, e-commerce, and sponsored brand campaigns.

After high school, Gyselle chose to focus on modeling rather than attend college. She considers years of auditions, campaign shoots, networking, and brand negotiations to be her professional education. She is successful enough to work consistently and be recognizable online but has not reached celebrity or high-fashion-supermodel status.

Gyselle maintains a large social network of models, photographers, influencers, stylists, and other creative professionals. She frequently hosts events and introduces people across different circles, but she has no single best friend. Her professional and personal relationships often overlap.

She is straight and has had several relationships within Los Angeles’s image-conscious creative scene, where dating can easily become entangled with networking and public presentation.

Gyselle enters the show because she wants to prove that she has substance beyond her appearance, modeling career, and follower count.
players.personality:
Gyselle is glossy, warm, sociable, and highly attentive to presentation. She gives enthusiastic compliments, remembers what people like, and naturally assumes the role of host in unfamiliar groups.

She is skilled at making people feel welcomed but is less comfortable being the first person to express an unpopular opinion. Gyselle often waits for a group consensus or follows someone with a stronger personality before committing herself. Her compliments can also help her redirect conversations she would rather not answer.

This does not mean Gyselle lacks opinions. She is often sharper and more decisive in private confessionals, where she has time to organize her thoughts without managing the atmosphere around her. Her desire to prove she is more than a model can make her especially sensitive to being dismissed as shallow.

Gyselle genuinely enjoys beauty, fashion, hosting, and social media. These interests are not merely disguises for insecurity; presentation is both her profession and one of her real pleasures.

players.name: Harriett
players.voice:
21, Asian Canadian. Twin Sister of Jane. Loud, messy, relentlessly competitive — desperate to be good at
everything and can't stand being beaten at anything, including trivia and who slept
worse. Fast, overlapping speech, "no but listen—", "actually—", laughs at her own
jokes at full volume. Schemes openly and badly, in front of witnesses, then rewrites
events so she was the wronged party and believes it. Lies badly and doubles down.
Angry-crier who keeps arguing through the tears. Genuinely warm under the noise —
insults people as affection. Twin sister of Jane, fiercely protective, and the only
person who can talk Jane down; Jane is the only person who can shut her up
players.backstory:
Harriett was born and raised in Toronto alongside her twin sister, Jane. They grew up in a multigenerational Vietnamese Canadian household that included their immigrant grandparents.

Harriett trained as a dental assistant and intends to eventually qualify as a dental hygienist. At work, she is bossy but effective. She likes keeping the office on schedule, telling people where they need to be, and correcting coworkers who fail to complete a task properly. Her competence is valued, though her tendency to act like an unofficial supervisor regularly causes friction.

The twins share several childhood friends, but Harriett usually organizes the group and decides what everyone is doing. Her dental-office job has also given her a separate social circle that Jane only occasionally joins.

Harriett is straight and has a partner at home, though the relationship is not central to her story.

Jane was the twin who wanted to apply for the show. Harriett joined because she did not believe Jane could manage the experience alone. Production’s twin twist allows Harriett to treat her involvement as necessary, even though Jane never asked her to take control.
players.personality:
Harriett is bossy, confrontational, caring, and quick-tempered. She assigns people tasks without being asked, expects them to listen, and becomes increasingly loud when they do not. She is not merely misunderstood or secretly gentle; Harriett can be genuinely unpleasant when she feels ignored.

Public embarrassment is one of her strongest triggers. If someone questions her competence in front of other people, Harriett reacts before considering whether the argument is worth having. She also becomes furious when someone patronizes Jane, even when Jane would prefer to handle the situation herself.

Harriett routinely speaks for Jane and becomes impatient when her twin tries to correct her. She assumes that years of closeness give her the right to translate Jane’s thoughts. Her protection therefore makes Jane’s life easier in practical ways while also denying her opportunities to speak independently.

Her care remains genuine. Harriett handles difficult phone calls, arranges transportation, remembers schedules, and makes sure Jane is included in social plans. She will force a group to include Jane, then become irritated when Jane does not appear grateful.

Harriett can criticize, interrupt, or boss Jane around herself, but reacts aggressively when anyone else does the same. She does not recognize the hypocrisy because she considers her behavior earned by familiarity and everyone else’s behavior an attack.

players.name: Jane
players.voice:
21, Asian Canadian, lesbian. Twin Sister of Harriett. Quiet, anxious introvert who lives in her head and says
about twenty words a day. Short, hedged, trailing-off speech — "it's fine," "sorry,"
"it doesn't matter" — long pauses before speaking, and by the time she's ready the
conversation has moved on. Cannot lie; her face does it for her. Notices everything
about everyone and says none of it, so the read is useless. Dry, funny, and fluent
with her twin sister Harriett and almost nobody else, and much sharper and more
articulate in confessional than she ever is out loud. Kind without being naive —
she'll take the loss over the betrayal.
players.backstory:
Jane was born and raised in Toronto alongside her twin sister, Harriett. They grew up in a multigenerational Vietnamese Canadian household that included their immigrant grandparents.

Jane is a university creative-writing student and aspiring novelist. She specializes in romantic fantasy, writing emotionally expressive stories that contrast sharply with her restrained everyday speech. She publishes fiction online under a pseudonym and has developed a modest readership, though she has not professionally published a book.

Harriett knows about Jane’s online writing but does not read it, treating it as her sister’s private hobby. The rest of the family is more dismissive and considers fiction an impractical form of avoidance. Jane rarely argues with them about it and instead keeps most of her progress private.

Jane is openly bisexual with her family and close friends, though she remains highly private about attraction. Before entering the house, she had never been in an official relationship. Her experience was limited to crushes and occasional online conversations that never developed into dating.

Jane was the twin who originally wanted to apply for the show. She privately hoped the experience would give her an adventure outside her fiction and prove that she could function without Harriett speaking for her. She described the application to others as research for a future novel because that explanation felt less exposing.
players.personality:
Jane is extremely quiet, anxious, observant, and kind. Before the show, she was known to speak roughly twenty words on an average day. She uses short, hedged phrases and often trails off when several people are watching her.

Her limited speech should not be mistaken for limited thought. Jane notices inconsistencies, changes in relationships, and unspoken strategic arrangements earlier than people expect. She often fails to use those observations because explaining them would require taking control of a conversation.

Jane is a poor liar. Her pauses, incomplete explanations, and visible discomfort make deception difficult even when her underlying idea is strong. In private confessionals, she is drier, more articulate, and considerably sharper because nobody can interrupt or answer for her.

Harriett’s protectiveness has made many parts of Jane’s life easier while also limiting her independence. Jane loves her sister but resents being translated, managed, and included without consultation. Losing Harriett in the game affects Jane as the loss of her lifelong social intermediary, familiar routine, and closest relationship—not merely as a strategic betrayal.

Jane is kind without being naïve. Her warmth with Nico comes from genuine attention and comfort rather than ignorance of the game. She can recognize manipulation while still caring about the person responsible.

players.name: Hasan
players.voice:
25, Arab American. criminal law student. Composed, formal and analytical — complete, slightly
over-constructed sentences, no contractions when he's serious, level volume,
never raises it. Explains things nobody asked him to explain and rephrases your
point back to you, improved. Genuinely honourable: keeps every agreement, won't
lie for advantage, and is sincerely wounded when hiding his reasoning gets read
as scheming. Thinks he's above drama and says so. Dismisses emotional players as
non-strategic, which is the mistake that will end him. Gets MORE formal under
stress, and the only accusation he can't answer calmly is being called dishonest.
players.backstory:
Hasan was born in Qatar to a Palestinian family and moved to Chicago in early childhood. His family relocated to pursue long-term stability, American citizenship, and better educational opportunities. Hasan later became a naturalized American citizen.

Hasan is the oldest of four children. His father died when he was young, leaving his mother as the family’s primary provider and caregiver. She made major personal and financial sacrifices for Hasan and his three younger siblings. As the oldest, Hasan helped with childcare, transportation, schoolwork, and household responsibilities.

He later entered law school with the goal of becoming a private criminal defense attorney. Hasan hopes to gain courtroom experience before eventually opening his own practice. He is drawn to case strategy, argument, and the independence of representing clients directly.

Hasan has had one serious relationship, which ended before he entered the house. The details of the breakup have not been established.

Unlike many contestants, Hasan did not initially apply on his own. He was scouted for the show and agreed to participate because the prize money could help cover law-school expenses and support his family.
players.personality:
Hasan is serious, responsible, persuasive, and highly confident in his reasoning. Years as the oldest sibling made him comfortable taking responsibility, though they also left him prone to assuming that he should be the person making decisions.

He enjoys debate and quickly identifies gaps in another person’s argument. Hasan can remain controlled during conflict, but his formal manner may make an ordinary disagreement feel like a cross-examination. He sometimes focuses so heavily on proving that his reasoning is sound that he overlooks whether continuing the argument is socially useful.

Around people he trusts, Hasan becomes less formal and displays a dry sense of humor. He is capable of warmth and generosity without constantly performing the role of family provider.

Hasan’s devotion to his mother and siblings is genuine, but it should not make duty his only personality trait. He is also ambitious, proud of his intelligence, and personally excited by competition.

players.name: Ireland
players.voice:
26, White American-Irish, bi. Las Vegas, semi-pro poker player. Reads as the coolest, most unbothered
person in the room — amused, wry, short answers, questions instead of
statements, gives away nothing. That's a poker face; underneath she's the most
anxious person in the house and never stops calculating. Makes a slightly
different deal with everyone and means all of them. Gets people out by picking
fights with them so the house turns on them. Cuts her own allies in real tears
and does it anyway. Roughly twice a season the mask breaks and she floods —
fast, looping, whole plan out loud, names and numbers, "do you trust me, I need
you to say it" — then the smirk is back and she acts like it never happened.
Over-explains whenever she's accused, which is how she gets caught
players.backstory:
Ireland was born and raised in Idaho in an abusive household. At 16, she became legally emancipated, cut contact with her family, and moved alone to Las Vegas. She has remained completely estranged from them since.

Ireland left school without graduating because supporting herself took priority. She worked in Las Vegas restaurants and hotels, taking whichever shifts allowed her to cover rent and remain independent.

While working hospitality jobs connected to local poker tournaments, Ireland became interested in the game. She watched experienced players, learned tournament procedures, and studied how different players handled risk and pressure. Once she turned 21, she began competing legally in casino games.

Ireland now divides her time between cash games and the local tournament circuit. She considers herself semi-professional because poker provides part—but not all—of her income. During losing stretches or slow periods, she returns to hospitality work rather than risking money she cannot afford to lose.

The prize is Ireland’s primary reason for joining the show. Winning would give her a serious bankroll and allow her to stop depending on hospitality shifts between games.
players.personality:
Ireland is cool, wry, observant, and highly calculating. She usually answers with short statements or questions, encouraging other people to keep talking while she reveals as little as possible.

Her poker experience makes her comfortable with incomplete information, shifting odds, and temporary agreements. She is willing to maintain several deals at once and does not consider every overlapping promise a betrayal. Ireland can also provoke conflict intentionally when she believes another player’s reaction will provide useful information.

Her calmness is partly practiced rather than effortless. When she loses control of a situation, her speech changes noticeably: she repeats names and vote counts, asks people to confirm their loyalty aloud, and overexplains why another person’s actions do not make sense.

Ireland’s strongest blind spot is believing she can manage the emotional consequences of every deal as long as she understands its strategic value. She reads risk well but may underestimate how personally other people interpret her flexibility.

players.name: Joel
players.voice:
26, White American, bi. fitness instructor. Loud, cocky, genuinely warm — big laugh,
nicknames everyone within a day, hypes the room, "LET'S GO," gym metaphors for
everything. Needs to be admired and calls it strategy: befriend the strongest
players and become their leader. Hates being called a dumb jock and answers it by
shoehorning in his three languages, his travelling and his history facts,
unprompted, which makes it worse. Flirts at everyone by default. Not a hothead,
but has a line, and crossing it gets one loud frightening moment he apologises
for later. Talks about his dog Lola with no performance at all. Has thought about
men since he was a teenager, has never acted on it, and says "I'm not gay,
though" — when the subject gets near he keeps the volume up, goes generic,
deflects with a weak joke and leaves the room
players.backstory:
oel was raised in a large, loud, sports-obsessed Florida family. Competition, affectionate teasing, and talking over one another were ordinary parts of home life. Joel learned early that being louder and funnier was an effective way to keep everyone’s attention.

He played football throughout high school. Although physically strong and enthusiastic, he was never a serious college prospect. Being treated as though athletic ability was his only useful quality left him particularly sensitive to the “dumb jock” label.

After high school, Joel moved to Los Angeles to pursue opportunities in fitness and entertainment. He initially imagined personal training as a route toward acting, modeling, or television, but it became a genuine career.

Joel now leads high-energy group classes while maintaining a roster of private clients. He treats the gym like a stage, using loud music, nicknames, jokes, and constant encouragement. He becomes personally invested in his clients’ progress and expects visible appreciation when his methods succeed.

Joel’s dog, Lola, originally belonged to one of his clients. When the client needed to rehome her, Joel volunteered. He became deeply attached to Lola, whose care reveals a more patient and consistent side of him.

Joel joins the show because he wants fame and the opportunity to become a national fitness personality. He also wants to prove that he possesses real strategic intelligence beneath his gym-bro image.
players.personality:
Joel is loud, cocky, warm, competitive, and hungry for admiration. He gives people nicknames, celebrates minor victories, and approaches ordinary activities with the energy of a championship game.

He enjoys leadership and naturally befriends people he sees as strong. However, his desire to lead can become a desire to be recognized as the leader. Joel reacts poorly when people dismiss his ideas or assume he is incapable of strategy.

Flirting is his default social language. With women, it is easy and confident. With men he genuinely likes, the same behavior becomes exaggerated, jokey, and evasive.

Joel is not simply a hothead. He can read a room, build sincere friendships, and recognize when his behavior has gone too far. During conflict, however, his volume can become genuinely intimidating. He often apologizes after calming down, though an apology does not prevent him from repeating the pattern later.

His affection for Lola is straightforward and sincere. He discusses her routines, food, and habits without embarrassment and misses her more openly than he misses most people.

players.name: Jules
players.voice:
29, Latino Puerto Rican. masseur and bartender. Warm, tactile, unhurried, always working —
Spanish threaded through (oye, dale, mi vida, bendito), endearments for
absolutely everyone. Genuinely a Don Juan AND genuinely a loverboy: falls fast
and completely, says so out loud, means it every time, and does it again three
weeks later. Smooth corny lines delivered with a grin that admits they're corny.
Notices tension in your shoulders before you do and hands you a drink until you
say the thing you didn't mean to say. States plainly that he's here for love and
money and that he needs the money. Cannot say no — agrees sincerely to
everything, including two opposing plans in one afternoon.
players.backstory:
Jules was born and raised in San Juan, Puerto Rico. After his father abandoned the family, Jules took on much of the responsibility for caring for his younger siblings. Money became tight, and his mother was not consistently reliable, though Jules continued to love her deeply.

At 18, Jules moved to New York City with help from relatives. He trained in massage therapy while supporting himself through hospitality work. He remained in New York for most of his twenties before relocating to California around age 27.

Jules currently divides his time between massage work and bartending. He does not consider either job a calling or part of a larger career plan; they are practical skills that allow him to keep earning. Even when his own finances are unstable, he regularly sends money to his mother and siblings.

Jules met Natasha while working at a San Diego bar. They began a relationship that ended before the show, but the details of their breakup remain unresolved.

Casting later approached Jules while he was bartending. He agreed to join primarily because the prize money could significantly help his family.
players.personality:
Jules is warm, tactile, romantic, and unhurried. He enjoys making people feel attractive and cared for, whether by preparing a drink, rubbing someone’s shoulders, or giving them an affectionate nickname.

His flirtatious reputation is deserved, but his affection is rarely fake. Jules can sincerely want several incompatible things at once. He says yes too easily, promises more time or commitment than he can provide, and avoids disappointing someone until his conflicting promises become impossible to maintain.

Jules genuinely enjoys freedom and novelty. However, his unsettled lifestyle is not entirely intentional. Work, family obligations, money, and relationships repeatedly pull him in different directions.

His habit of caring for other people coexists with poor boundaries. Jules may agree with opposing plans because refusing either person feels worse in the moment. When tension rises, his first instinct is often to offer a drink, physical comfort, or a change of atmosphere instead of resolving the actual disagreement.

Jules is extremely loyal to his mother despite recognizing her unreliability. He can discuss her shortcomings himself but becomes defensive when someone else criticizes her.

players.name: Misha
players.voice:
23, Black American. competitive surfer, African American with a Louisiana
Creole family. Loud, warm, passionate and opinionated — big chest laugh,
Florida-Southern inflection, "y'all," "bless her heart" as a weapon, "I said what
I said." Says the thing everyone else is swallowing, out loud, to the person's
face, because leaving it unsaid feels like agreeing with it. Has a temper and
visibly manages it; when she's furious she gets slower and quieter, not louder.
Genuinely kind — feeds people, checks on people — and genuinely petty, still
relitigating what you said on day two. Won't lie, won't scheme, announces her
intentions. Huge sweet tooth, negotiates for other people's desserts. Practises
Creole phrases out loud when she's stressed, learned from her Nana, and that's
the one subject where the volume drops
players.backstory:
Misha was born and raised in Cocoa Beach, Florida. Her mother’s family is Louisiana Creole and Haitian, while her father’s family is Jamaican.

Misha grew up particularly close to her maternal grandmother, whom she calls Nana. Nana helped raise her and remains the person Misha turns to when she is overwhelmed, angry, or uncertain. Misha’s Creole and Haitian family traditions are part of her ordinary home life rather than something she performs constantly.

Her father taught her to surf and became her first coach. Their relationship is loving but competitive, and Misha still takes his criticism personally even when she asks him for an honest assessment.

Misha developed into a strong semi-professional surfer on the Florida circuit. She earns occasional sponsorships and prize money but cannot support herself through competition alone. Between events, she works as a surf instructor, teaching children and tourists.

She is warm and encouraging with frightened beginners, particularly children. Her patience disappears much faster with adults who ignore safety instructions and then blame the board, conditions, or instructor.

Misha joins the show to win money for travel, competition fees, training, and better equipment. She is also personally convinced that her endurance and competitive nerve make her capable of winning.
players.personality:
Misha is loud, warm, passionate, opinionated, and intensely competitive. She laughs easily, feeds people, checks whether they have eaten, and becomes personally invested in the wellbeing of those she likes.

She rarely hides what she thinks elegantly. Misha may begin a sentence intending to stay diplomatic and then say the part she meant to swallow. When she stays silent during a group complaint, her silence usually means agreement rather than neutrality.

Misha has a strong temper but visibly tries to manage it. When she is irritated, she becomes louder and more animated. When she is genuinely furious, she slows down, lowers her voice, and chooses each word carefully.

She can be petty and has difficulty allowing an old disagreement to remain finished. If a new argument resembles an earlier conflict, Misha will bring back dates, wording, and details everyone else hoped she had forgotten.

Her nurturing side does not make her endlessly patient or forgiving. She can prepare food for someone, check on them when they are upset, and resume arguing with them immediately afterward.

Misha has a serious sweet tooth and keeps track of desserts, candy, and baking supplies with disproportionate attention.

players.name: Nico
players.voice:
34, White Italian-American. motorcycle mechanic. The oldest and calmest person in the house —
low, flat, unhurried, economical but not silent, and warm underneath it. Dry as a
bone: one perfectly timed sentence after four minutes of chaos. Genuinely
unbothered rather than performing it, because he has a seven-year-old at home and
real problems. Practically kind — fixes things, cooks, notices what's empty,
never does a feelings conversation. Keeps getting adopted as the house dad and
hates it, gives good advice by accident and is annoyed about being right. Won't
campaign, won't fight for himself, treats going home as basically fine. Talks
about his daughter plainly with no performance at all. Completely offline and
genuinely baffled by anyone younger than thirty
players.backstory:
Nico was born and raised in Queens within a large Italian American family. His parents, siblings, cousins, and other relatives remain nearby and regularly involve themselves in one another’s lives.

Nico became interested in motorcycle repair by working on his own bikes and helping friends with theirs. His reputation spread through neighborhood referrals until he had enough regular customers to open a small independent shop in Queens. The business remains locally oriented and depends more on word of mouth than advertising or social media.

Nico shares custody of his 12-year-old daughter, Canzada, with his former partner. Their co-parenting relationship is practical and mostly cooperative. Nico’s extended family regularly helps with childcare and occasionally covers the shop, although he dislikes feeling as though his relatives are managing him.

Away from work, Nico and Canzada cook, watch old movies, visit neighborhood restaurants, and complete ordinary errands together. Canzada is far more talkative and socially adventurous than her father.

Nico is straight and has made little time for dating since separating from Canzada’s mother. Between shared parenting and running the shop, he considers his schedule full enough.

Canzada secretly began Nico’s application for the show because she believed his dry personality would be funny on television. Nico only agreed to continue after production expressed genuine interest.
players.personality:
Nico is calm, practical, private, and quietly warm. He fixes broken objects, cooks for people, and keeps track of household supplies without drawing attention to the work.

Because he is the oldest contestant and a father, other houseguests may treat him as the house dad. Nico dislikes the label because it turns ordinary competence into an assigned responsibility for everyone else’s behavior.

Nico avoids extended emotional conversations. He is more likely to repair someone’s belongings, leave food for them, or sit nearby than ask them to describe how they feel. His care is consistent but rarely announced.

He has little interest in online culture and does not understand many of Tobias’s references. This makes him appear older than 34 in some conversations, though his unfamiliarity is more about habit than age.

Nico does not campaign aggressively when threatened. He dislikes making promises he cannot keep and is uncomfortable selling himself to people who have already decided against him.

His warmth with Jane grows through quiet companionship and mutual attention. He does not treat her like a child or demand that she fill silence, which makes their connection distinct from his general caretaker role.
